items.note: A similar statement is in Lau's work; the differences are that p ≥ 3 is not assumed and that the underlying A_inf-module is given by an explicit formula. It is the result used by Česnavičius–Scholze on purity for flat cohomology.

items.name: Torsion-freeness of the prismatic cohomology of a syntomic algebra
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism with A p-torsion free, and let S be a p-completely syntomic A/I-algebra (i.e. S/p ≅ S ⊗^L_{A/I} (A/I)/p and (A/I)/p → S/p is syntomic). Then H^0(S, Δ_{S/A}) is p-torsion free.
items.note: A general statement about prismatic cohomology proved here; PR.1 and PR.2 own prismatic cohomology and its torsion behaviour, so the paper is a source for those layers.

items.name: Cartier duality for finite locally free group schemes
items.statement: Let H be a finite locally free group scheme of p-power order over a quasi-syntomic ring R. There is a natural isomorphism τ_{≤1}RHom_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}H, O_Δ)^∨[−1] ≃ τ_{≤1}RHom_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}Ȟ, O_Δ), where (−)^∨ = RHom_{O_Δ}(−, O_Δ). When R is perfectoid, Hom_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}H, O_Δ) = 0, so that in degree 1 one obtains Ext^1_{O_Δ}(Ext^1_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}H, O_Δ), O_Δ) ≃ Ext^1_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}Ȟ, O_Δ) and therefore Ext^1_{Δ_R}(M_Δ(H), Δ_R) ≃ M_Δ(Ȟ), expressing the compatibility of M_Δ with Cartier duality on finite locally free group schemes of p-power order over R.
items.locator: arXiv:1907.10525v4 (11 October 2022), Remark 5.1.7 (not in the published version)
items.note: The crystalline analogue is Berthelot–Breen–Messing Theorem 5.2.7. This remark is present in arXiv v4 and absent from the published version, which passes directly from Remark 5.6 to the discussion of the Breuil–Kisin case; it is the only place where the two versions differ in content, and it is recorded here so that the design job plans the duality statement.

items.name: Quasi-syntomic perfectoid covers of regular local rings
items.statement: Let R be a complete Noetherian local ring with perfect residue field of characteristic p. If R is regular, then there exists a quasi-syntomic perfectoid cover R_∞ of R.
items.note: Built from Bhatt–Iyengar–Ma's faithfully flat perfectoid cover of a regular ring, refined here to a quasi-syntomic cover by a cotangent-complex computation. PerfectoidSpaces P7 owns Frobenius-controlled towers and their perfectoid completions, and the extraction of Česnavičius's purity paper already proposes adding Cohen-structure regular finite-flat towers there; the paper is a source for that layer.

items.name: Automatic admissibility over a complete regular local ring
items.statement: Let R be a complete regular local ring with perfect residue field of characteristic p. Then every prismatic Dieudonné crystal over R is admissible.
items.note: This is why over such rings the classification can be stated without the admissibility condition; the general functor without admissibility is not essentially surjective.

items.name: Comparison with the Breuil–Kisin classification
items.statement: Let R be a complete regular local ring with perfect residue field of characteristic p, and let (A, I) be the associated Breuil–Kisin prism. The functor BT(R) → BK_min(A), G ↦ v^*M_Δ(G)((A,I)) = Ext^1_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}G, O_Δ)_{(A,I)}, is an equivalence of categories.
items.note: Over R = O_K this is the Breuil–Kisin classification as extended to all p by Kim, Lau and Liu; here it is proved for all complete regular local rings with perfect residue field. R07.4 plans the classification of p-divisible groups by Breuil–Kisin modules over the base fields used by Kisin, including the dyadic case, but not this prismatic proof nor the extension beyond discrete valuation rings, and the functor here is defined through the prismatic site.

items.name: The Breuil–Kisin prism covers the final object
items.statement: The natural map from the sheaf represented by the Breuil–Kisin prism (A, I) to the final object of Shv((R)_Δ) is an epimorphism for the p-completely faithfully flat topology.
items.note: The covering statement that makes evaluation on the Breuil–Kisin prism faithful.

items.name: Topological nilpotence over the Breuil–Kisin prism
items.statement: With the notation from the proof of the comparison theorem, the ideal J ⊆ B is contained in N^{≥1}B, is stable by φ_1 := φ/E(u), and φ_1 is topologically nilpotent on J for the (p, E)-adic topology.
items.note: The hypothesis that lets the window equivalence along a nilpotent surjection be applied to the Breuil–Kisin prism and its self-product.

items.name: Prismatic F-crystals over O_K and crystalline lattices
items.statement: Prismatic Dieudonné crystals over O_K are the same as minuscule Breuil–Kisin modules, but the analogous statement fails for non-minuscule finite locally free F-crystals on the absolute prismatic site of O_K: the descent datum has to be remembered. Bhatt and Scholze prove that finite locally free F-crystals on the absolute prismatic site of O_K are the same as Gal_K-stable lattices in crystalline representations of Gal_K; in the minuscule case this recovers, with the results above, the equivalence between p-divisible groups over O_K and Gal_K-stable lattices in crystalline representations with Hodge–Tate weights in {0,1}.
items.note: PR.7 proves exactly the Bhatt–Scholze equivalence for Spf(O_K) and compares the evaluation on the Breuil–Kisin prism with R07's Kisin functor, including uniformizer dependence; the warning that a finite locally free F-crystal is not determined by its underlying Breuil–Kisin module is PR.7's own caveat.

items.name: Comparison over the PD thickening S
items.statement: There is a natural Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism α_K : M_Δ(G)(S, (p)) ≅ D(G)(S), where D(G)(S) is the evaluation of the crystalline Dieudonné crystal of G at the PD thickening S → O_K.
items.note: The comparison used to identify the prismatic functor with Kisin's.

items.name: Kisin's functor is the prismatic one
items.statement: The two functors G ↦ M^Kis(G) and G ↦ M_Δ(G)(𝔖, (E)) from p-divisible groups over O_K to minuscule Breuil–Kisin modules are naturally isomorphic.
items.note: The identification of the new classification with the classical one. PR.7 plans the comparison of the evaluation of an F-crystal on the Breuil–Kisin prism with R07's Kisin functor for crystalline representations; the statement here is the Dieudonné-theoretic counterpart, defined through M_Δ, and belongs with it.

items.name: Display
items.statement: Let R be a p-complete ring. A display over R is a window over the frame W(O) = (W(O), I(O) := ker(W(O) → O), F, F_1) in the topos of sheaves on the p-completely faithfully flat site of R, where F is the Witt vector Frobenius and F_1 : I(O) → W(O) is the inverse of the bijective Verschiebung morphism V. The category of displays over R is Disp(R).
items.note: Zink's displays, phrased here as windows over a frame of sheaves. Mathlib has Witt vectors with their Frobenius and Verschiebung (WittVector.frobenius, WittVector.verschiebung), but nothing in the atlas plans displays: a search of the layer descriptions returns no occurrence of the notion.

items.name: Displays satisfy p-completely faithfully flat descent
items.statement: The category of displays satisfies faithfully flat descent. Since displays over a p-complete ring R with bounded p^∞-torsion are equivalent to compatible systems of displays over R/p^n for all n ≥ 1, displays even satisfy p-completely faithfully flat descent; hence the category of displays over R in the sense above is the usual category of displays, i.e. of windows over the frame (W(R), I(R), F, F_1).
items.note: The comparison of the abstract sheaf-theoretic definition with Zink's; it is what makes the comparison theorem a statement about the classical notion.

items.name: The frame morphism from the Nygaard frame to the Witt frame
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring and assume that pR = 0 or that R is p-torsion free. The natural morphism Δ_R → R, given by dividing out N^{≥1}Δ_R, lifts to a u-morphism of frames f : Δ_{R,Nyg} → W(R), where Δ_{R,Nyg} is the frame associated to (Δ_R, I) and ξ̃, and u ∈ W(R) is a unit with p = u f(ξ̃).
items.note: The bridge between prismatic Dieudonné theory and displays: the map Δ_R → W(R) obtained by adjunction from θ : Δ_R → R carries N^{≥1}Δ_R into the image of Verschiebung.

items.name: The display of a p-divisible group
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-syntomic ring. For a p-divisible group G over R set Z_R(G) = M_Δ(G) ⊗_{O^pris} W(O) with Frobenius F_{Z_R(G)} = φ_{M_Δ(G)} ⊗ F, and let Fil Z_R(G) be the submodule generated by I(O)·Z_R(G) and the image of φ_{M_Δ(G)}^{-1}(I^pris·M_Δ(G)). There is a unique way to extend G ↦ (Z_R(G), Fil Z_R(G), F_{Z_R(G)}) to a functor Z_R : BT(R) → Disp(R) natural in R which moreover coincides, through the window description of admissibility, with the composition of the prismatic Dieudonné functor with the functor induced by the frame morphism above when R is quasi-regular semiperfectoid and pR = 0 or R is p-torsion free.
items.note: The construction of Zink's display out of the prismatic Dieudonné crystal.

items.name: Formal p-divisible groups and nilpotent displays
items.statement: Let R be a quasi-syntomic ring, flat over Z/p^n for some n > 0 or over Z_p. The functor Z_R restricts to an antiequivalence BT_f(R) ≅ Disp_nilp(R) between the category of formal p-divisible groups over R and the category of F-nilpotent displays over R (a display is F-nilpotent if its Frobenius is nilpotent modulo p). This reproves the main result of Lau and Zink in the special case of quasi-syntomic rings.
items.note: This is the proposition whose proof the 2025 erratum retracts: the key step, that the divided Frobenius acts topologically nilpotently on the kernel of A_crys(R) → W(R) for a quasi-regular semiperfect ring R, is false, and Andrew Senger's counterexample is recorded below as a source issue. The statement itself is unaffected, since it was already known by the different proofs of Zink and Lau cited immediately before it.

items.name: Frobenius fixed points of the prismatic structure sheaf
items.statement: The morphisms α : Spa(R[1/p], R)^♦_v → (R)_{qsyn,qrsp} and j induce natural isomorphisms α_*(Z/p^n) ≅ (O^pris/p^n)^{φ=1} and (α ∘ j)_*(Z/p^n) ≅ (O^pris/p^n[1/I])^{φ=1} of sheaves on (R)_{qsyn,qrsp} after passing to φ-fixed points.
items.note: The sheaf-theoretic form of the étale comparison. PR.4 constructs the comparison from generic-fibre Z/p^n étale cohomology to (Δ/p^n[1/I])^{φ=1} for a perfect base prism and a smooth formal scheme, and insists that φ = 1 be a derived fixed-point construction; the statement here is on the quasi-syntomic site and for arbitrary quasi-syntomic R, so it is not the same statement.

items.name: Étale comparison for the prismatic Dieudonné crystal
items.statement: Let G be a p-divisible group over R with prismatic Dieudonné crystal M_Δ(G) and let n ≥ 0. Then j^*α^*(M_Δ(G)/p^n[1/I]^{φ=1}) is canonically isomorphic to Hom_{Z/p^n}(G[p^n]_η, Z/p^n), where G[p^n]_η denotes the sheaf Spa(S[1/p], S) ↦ G[p^n](S[1/p]) on Spa(R[1/p], R)^♦_v.
items.note: The recovery of the generic-fibre Tate module from the prismatic Dieudonné crystal, which is the p-divisible-group case of the étale comparison planned in PR.4.

items.name: Pullback of the finite flat group scheme to the generic fibre
items.statement: With the notation above, (α ∘ j)^*G[p^n] ≅ G[p^n]_η.
items.note: The compatibility making the previous statement meaningful.

items.name: Finite projective modules over a derived p-complete ring
items.statement: Let R be a derived p-complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion. Then the natural functor {finite projective R-modules} → 2-lim_n {finite projective R/p^n-modules} is an equivalence. In particular, the fibered category R ↦ {finite projective R-modules} is a stack for the p-completely faithfully flat topology on derived p-complete rings with bounded p^∞-torsion.
items.note: A descent statement for finite projective modules on p-complete rings; PR.2 proves derived complete-flat descent and the base-change formulas in that setting, so the paper is a source for that layer.

items.name: p-divisible groups form a stack for the p-completely flat topology
items.statement: The fibered categories of p-divisible groups and of finite locally free group schemes over p-complete rings with bounded p^∞-torsion are stacks for the p-completely faithfully flat topology.
items.note: The descent statement for the source category of the main theorem. R07.1 owns finite locally free group schemes, p-divisible groups and fpqc descent for them; the p-completely faithfully flat version over p-complete rings with bounded p^∞-torsion is proved here, so the paper is a source for that layer.

items.name: Descent of finite projective modules along faithfully flat maps of prisms
items.statement: The fibered category (A, I) ↦ {finite projective A-modules} on the category of bounded prisms is a stack for the faithfully flat topology.
items.note: The descent statement for the target category; it is what makes prismatic Dieudonné crystals a stack. In the same layer as the first appendix item.

items.name: A classically (p,f)-complete ring with unbounded p-power torsion
items.statement: Set R := Z[f, x_{i,j} : i ≥ 0, 0 ≤ j ≤ i]^{∧(p,f)}/J with J generated by the elements p x_{i,j} − f x_{i,j+1}, where x_{i,i+1} := 0. Then f is a non-zero divisor in R and all p^∞-torsion in R/f ≅ Z[x_{i,j}]/(p x_{i,j}) is killed by p, but p^i x_{i,0} = p^{i−1} f x_{i,1} = … = f^i x_{i,i} ≠ 0 while p^{i+1}x_{i,0} = f^i p x_{i,i} = 0, so R has unbounded p^∞-torsion. Since f is a non-zero divisor, the (p,f)^∞-torsion in R is zero.
items.note: The counterexample showing that boundedness of p^∞-torsion does not descend along f, which is why the boundedness hypotheses on prisms are stated as they are. PR.0 and PR.2 make boundedness a standing hypothesis, so this example belongs with them. The printed chain has a misprint in its second term, recorded below as a source issue; the statement above is corrected.

prerequisites.citation: Eike Lau, Dieudonné theory over semiperfect rings and perfectoid rings, Compositio Math. 154 (2018), 1974–2004
prerequisites.why: The classification of p-divisible groups and of finite locally free group schemes of p-power order over a perfectoid ring, for p ≥ 3. It is one of the two sources of the perfectoid case that the main theorem takes as an input, and Theorem 5.4 of this paper is the statement of its Theorem 10.12 without the hypothesis p ≥ 3 and with an explicit formula for the underlying A_inf-module.

prerequisites.citation: Peter Scholze and Jared Weinstein, Berkeley Lectures on p-adic Geometry, Annals of Mathematics Studies 207, Princeton University Press (2020)
prerequisites.why: The Appendix to Lecture XVII constructs the functor M^SW classifying p-divisible groups over a perfectoid ring by Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules; the prismatic Dieudonné functor over a perfectoid ring is shown to be its naive dual, and this is the base case on which the whole proof rests.

prerequisites.citation: Bhargav Bhatt and Jacob Lurie, Absolute prismatic cohomology (2022)
prerequisites.why: Its Theorem 7.5.6 computes the Frobenius fixed points of the first Nygaard piece, giving the short exact sequence 0 → T_pG_m → N^{≥1}O^pris → O^pris → 0. That is the input from which T_pǦ is recovered from M_Δ(G), and hence the engine of the proof of full faithfulness.

prerequisites.citation: Thomas Zink, The display of a formal p-divisible group, Astérisque 278 (2002), 127–248
prerequisites.why: Displays, their faithfully flat descent, and the classification of formal p-divisible groups by nilpotent displays. Section 5.3 of this paper constructs the display of a p-divisible group from its prismatic Dieudonné crystal and reproves that classification for quasi-syntomic rings; nothing in the atlas plans displays.

prerequisites.citation: Eike Lau, Displays and formal p-divisible groups, Invent. Math. 171 (2008), 617–628
prerequisites.why: The other proof of the display classification of formal p-divisible groups. It is cited immediately before the display comparison of Section 5.3, and it is why the 2025 erratum can say that the retracted proof affects no result of the paper: the statement was already known from this and from Zink.

prerequisites.citation: Pierre Berthelot, Lawrence Breen and William Messing, Théorie de Dieudonné cristalline II, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 930, Springer (1982)
prerequisites.why: Crystalline Dieudonné theory: the crystalline Dieudonné crystal of a p-divisible group, with which Theorem 4.44 of this paper compares the prismatic one; the Hodge cohomology of an abelian scheme (2.5.2) and Raynaud's embedding theorem (3.1.1), which the computation of the Ext-sheaves rests on; and the crystalline Cartier duality (5.2.7) of which Remark 5.1.7 of the preprint is the prismatic analogue.

prerequisites.citation: William Messing, The crystals associated to Barsotti–Tate groups, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 264, Springer (1972)
prerequisites.why: The universal vector extension of a p-divisible group and the syntomicity of its finite levels G[p^n] over the base, which is what makes Hom(G, Q) vanish for a derived p-complete quasi-syntomic sheaf Q and hence makes Ext^1 the right invariant.

prerequisites.citation: Luc Illusie, Déformations de groupes de Barsotti–Tate (d'après A. Grothendieck), Astérisque 127 (1985), 151–198
prerequisites.why: Corollaire 2.2.5 characterises truncated Barsotti–Tate groups of level n by the coLie complex, and gives the dimension and the height of their pieces; it is the criterion used to prove that the prismatic Ext-sheaf of a BT_n is finite locally free over O_Δ/p^n.

prerequisites.citation: Bryden Cais and Eike Lau, Dieudonné crystals and Wach modules for p-divisible groups (2014)
prerequisites.why: Lemma 2.1.16 is the equivalence between windows over the frame attached to an oriented prism by the divided Frobenius with respect to φ(d) and minuscule Breuil–Kisin modules; it is the half of the window machinery that the Breuil–Kisin comparison of Section 5.2 is built on. Lemma 2.5.1 supplies the comparison of windows with Grothendieck's admissible filtrations in the quasi-regular semiperfect case.

Frames and windows in the generality used here, including the frame of Witt vectors over a sheaf of rings (its Example 5.4) that defines a display in Section 5.3, and the normal-decomposition machinery for windows.

prerequisites.citation: Bhargav Bhatt, Srikanth B. Iyengar and Linquan Ma, Regular rings and perfect(oid) algebras (2018)
prerequisites.why: Theorem 4.7 provides the faithfully flat perfectoid cover of a complete regular Noetherian local ring with perfect residue field, which Section 5.2 refines to a quasi-syntomic cover; the converse direction quoted there, that a Noetherian ring with p in its Jacobson radical admitting a faithfully flat perfectoid map is regular, is the paper's main theorem.

routes.title: Prismatic cohomology: relative, absolute, Nygaard and log variants, Part II: prismatic Dieudonné theory
routes.brief: Plan prismatic Dieudonné theory: the classification of p-divisible groups over a quasi-syntomic ring by admissible prismatic Dieudonné crystals, after Anschütz and Le Bras. The final theorems are their Theorem 1.13 and Theorem 1.16 of the published version (arXiv Theorems 1.4.1 and 1.4.4): for a quasi-syntomic ring R and a p-divisible group G over R, the pair (M_Δ(G) = Ext^1(G, O^pris), φ), where the Ext is taken in abelian sheaves on the small quasi-syntomic site of R and φ is induced by the Frobenius of O^pris, is an admissible prismatic Dieudonné crystal over R; and the resulting functor M_Δ : BT(R) → DM^adm(R) is an antiequivalence between p-divisible groups over R and admissible prismatic Dieudonné crystals over R. The roadmap must cover, in this order. (1) The coefficient sheaves: the morphisms of topoi u : Shv((R)_Δ) → Shv((R)_QSYN) and v, the exactness of u^{-1} on short exact sequences of abelian sheaves, the sheaves O^pris = v_*O_Δ, N^{≥1}O^pris and I^pris, the identification O^pris/N^{≥1}O^pris ≅ O, and the equivalence between finite locally free O_Δ-modules and finite locally free O^pris-modules. (2) The objects: prismatic Dieudonné crystals, the admissibility condition and its snake-lemma reformulation, the categories DM(R) and DM^adm(R), the stack property for the quasi-syntomic topology, prismatic Dieudonné modules over a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring and their identification with crystals by evaluation on the initial prism, the automatic admissibility over a perfectoid ring, and the earlier equivalent formulation by filtered prismatic Dieudonné crystals. (3) The frame and window language of Lau and Zink: frames, u-morphisms of frames, the two frames A_d and A_Nyg attached to an oriented prism, windows, α-morphisms and base change, normal decompositions, the identification Fil M = φ_M^{-1}(ϖM), and the two theorems that carry the argument — windows over A_d are minuscule Breuil–Kisin modules (Cais–Lau) and windows over Δ_{R,Nyg} are admissible prismatic Dieudonné modules — together with the equivalences and faithfulness statements along surjections on whose kernel the divided Frobenius is topologically nilpotent. (4) The functor: M_Δ(G) = Ext^1_{(R)_qsyn}(G, O^pris), the vanishing Hom(G, Q) = 0 for derived p-complete Q, the universal cover exact sequence and the resulting description M_Δ(G) ≅ Hom(T_pG, O^pris), and the comparisons — with the crystalline Dieudonné functor of Berthelot–Breen–Messing in characteristic p, with the classical Dieudonné module over a perfect field, and with the Scholze–Weinstein functor over a perfectoid ring. (5) The computation: Ext-groups in a topos through the functorial resolution C(G)_•, the prismatic cohomology of an abelian scheme and the degeneration of its conjugate spectral sequence, Raynaud's embedding of a finite locally free group scheme into an abelian scheme, and the resulting proof that M_Δ(G) is a finite locally free crystal of rank the height of G, with M_Δ(G)/Fil ≅ Lie(Ǧ). (6) The proof of the antiequivalence: the computation of M_Δ(Q_p/Z_p) and of M_Δ(μ_{p^∞}) through the q-logarithm and the Breuil–Kisin twist O_Δ{−1}, compatibility with Cartier duality, exactness, full faithfulness over a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring via T_pǦ ≅ ker(φ/ξ̃ − 1 : N^{≥1}M_Δ(G) → M_Δ(G)), essential surjectivity by descent from a perfectoid cover, and the explicit quasi-inverse M ↦ (M^∨)^{φ=1} ⊗ Q_p/Z_p. (7) The complements: torsion prismatic Dieudonné modules and the exact antiequivalence with finite locally free group schemes of p-power order over a perfectoid ring, with its Cartier duality; the comparison over a complete regular local ring with perfect residue field, recovering the Breuil–Kisin classification and identifying the prismatic functor with Kisin's M^Kis over O_K; the functor to Zink's displays and the antiequivalence between formal p-divisible groups and F-nilpotent displays; and the étale comparison recovering the generic-fibre Tate module. routes.reason: The atlas plans prisms and prismatic cohomology in depth — PrismaticCohomology PR.0 through PR.8 cover δ-rings and prisms, the relative and absolute sites, the Hodge–Tate, crystalline, de Rham and étale comparisons, the Nygaard filtration with its divided Frobenius and Breuil–Kisin twists, and prismatic F-crystals with their crystalline realization — and it plans p-divisible groups, classical Dieudonné theory and Breuil–Kisin modules in FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1, R07.2 and R07.4. What it does not plan anywhere is the object this paper constructs: the prismatic Dieudonné crystal M_Δ(G) = Ext^1(G, O^pris) of a p-divisible group, the sheaves O^pris, N^{≥1}O^pris and I^pris on the quasi-syntomic site, the morphism of topoi u that produces them, the admissibility condition, the frame-and-window language in which admissibility is handled, and the classification theorems. Searches of the layer descriptions return no occurrence of 'Dieudonné crystal' in the prismatic sense, of 'display' or of 'Barsotti–Tate' beyond R07.1's level structures. This is new mathematics in the direction PrismaticCohomology already goes: it uses PR.0's prisms, PR.1's site and comparisons, PR.2's derived and quasi-regular semiperfectoid theory, PR.3's Nygaard filtration and twists, PR.4's étale comparison and PR.5's absolute site as its whole technical apparatus, and its one new comparison with the outside world — prismatic F-crystals over O_K and crystalline lattices — is PR.7's theorem. So it is a Part II of PrismaticCohomology rather than a new roadmap. The alternative reading is that it is a Part II of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory, whose R07.2 is 'Dieudonné theory' and whose R07.4 is the Breuil–Kisin classification that Section 5.2 recovers; a reviewer who prefers that parent should say so, and the brief transfers unchanged, because the imports would simply be reversed. The case for PrismaticCohomology is that every object in the paper lives on a prismatic or quasi-syntomic site and that the p-divisible group is an input rather than the ambient subject, while R07 is organised around local fields and Galois representations; and that the paper is already a source of PR.0, PR.1 and PR.2 for its prism and prismatic-cohomology generalities, so keeping it in the same family avoids a roadmap that imports half of another roadmap's later layers.

Sections 2, 3 and 6 of the paper are a careful, self-contained account of the prism and prismatic-cohomology generalities that PR.0 to PR.3 plan, and they prove several statements in that range that Bhatt–Scholze do not. PR.0 constructs δ-rings, distinguished elements, prisms, orientations, boundedness and prismatic envelopes: the regularity of the sequences (p, φ^r(d)) and (φ^r(d), φ^s(d)) in a transversal prism, the explicit presentation of the envelope A{x/d}^{∧(p,d)} by the elements z_n with φ^n(d)φ^{n−1}(d)^p⋯d^{p^n}z_n = x^{p^n}, and the example of a classically (p,f)-complete ring with unbounded p^∞-torsion all belong there. PR.1 owns the relative site and the crystalline comparison: the paper extends Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 5.2 from p-completely smooth to p-completely syntomic algebras and then, by descent, to all quasi-syntomic F_p-algebras, and proves that H^0(S, Δ_{S/A}) is p-torsion free for a p-completely syntomic algebra over a p-torsion-free bounded prism. PR.2 owns derived prismatic cohomology, its conjugate filtration and derived complete-flat descent: the identification of Fil_1^conj Δ̄_{X/A} with the cotangent complex over Spf(A) and its consequence that this piece splits exactly when X lifts over A/I², the Künneth formula in both its algebraic and its geometric form, and the two appendix descent statements for finite projective modules over derived p-complete rings and over bounded prisms all belong there. The route also names four statements the paper proves that those layers already plan — that all reasonable prisms agree for a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring, that Δ_R ≅ A_crys(R) when pR = 0 with the Frobenius twist over W(R^♭) made explicit, and the identification of the graded pieces of the Nygaard filtration — because the paper is an unusually complete written source for them.

Q0's integral-algebra prefix owns integral perfectoid rings, their relation to Tate perfectoid rings and the A_inf and θ descriptions. The paper proves there that a p-completely étale algebra over a perfectoid ring is perfectoid, and that the p-completion of the henselization of a perfectoid ring along an ideal is perfectoid; the second statement is what lets a p-divisible group be lifted along a henselian pair in Section 4.6, and it is not part of the Bhatt–Scholze material Q0 already imports.

P7 owns Frobenius-controlled towers and their perfectoid completions, including the Cohen-structure regular finite-flat towers that the extraction of Česnavičius's purity paper proposes adding there. The statement here is of that kind: a complete regular Noetherian local ring with perfect residue field of characteristic p admits a perfectoid cover — Bhatt–Iyengar–Ma's theorem — which the paper refines to a quasi-syntomic cover by a cotangent-complex computation, unramified case first and then by a finite flat tower. It is what makes the Breuil–Kisin comparison of Section 5.2 possible, and it is a statement about perfectoid covers rather than about Dieudonné theory.

R07.1 owns finite locally free group schemes with their Cartier duality, connected–étale sequences, subgroups, quotients and fpqc descent, p-divisible groups as compatible finite locally free levels, and Raynaud's generic-fibre full-faithfulness theorem. Four statements the paper needs belong there and are not planned: Raynaud's other theorem, that a finite locally free group scheme embeds Zariski-locally into a projective abelian scheme (Berthelot–Breen–Messing 3.1.1), which is what makes the whole computation possible; Illusie's criterion recognising a truncated Barsotti–Tate group of level n by the coLie complex, with the dimension and height of its pieces; the lifting of a p-divisible group along a henselian pair; and the statement that p-divisible groups and finite locally free group schemes over p-complete rings with bounded p^∞-torsion are stacks for the p-completely faithfully flat topology, which is the descent the classification is proved by.

AI.2 constructs Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules over A_inf, their lattices, modifications and torsion decompositions, and proves Fargues' classification of the finite free ones over an algebraically closed C by pairs (T, Ξ) with Ξ a B_dR^+-lattice. The paper supplies two statements in that direction: that admissible prismatic Dieudonné modules over a perfectoid ring are exactly the minuscule Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules — the dictionary by which Lau's and Scholze–Weinstein's classifications become the perfectoid case of the main theorem — and that a minuscule Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module over O_C is determined by the triple (T_M, M_crys, α_M) consisting of its Frobenius-invariant Z_p-lattice, its crystalline realization and the comparison isomorphism over B_crys. The second is the crystalline companion of Fargues' de Rham description and belongs beside it.

A4 constructs the relative H^1_dR of an abelian scheme with its Hodge exact sequence, Gauss–Manin connection, cup product and base change, and says explicitly that these are degree-one statements. The input this paper needs, Berthelot–Breen–Messing 2.5.2, is the whole package: for every k, i and j the modules H^k(X, Ω^•_{X/Ā}) and H^i(X, Ω^j_{X/Ā}) are finite locally free and commute with base change, and the canonical map ∧^*H^1(X, Ω^•_{X/Ā}) → H^*(X, Ω^•_{X/Ā}) is an isomorphism of algebras. That exterior structure is what makes the prismatic Ext-sheaf of an abelian scheme finite locally free of rank 2 dim(X), and it is the natural completion of A4's degree-one statements.

sourceIssues.printed: We claim that the divided Frobenius is topologically nilpotent on its kernel. It suffices to show the same for the surjection A_crys(R) → W(R) coming from the PD-thickening W(R) → R. We recall that A_crys(R) is obtained from W(R^♭) by passing to the PD-envelope for the ideal ker(W(R^♭) → R). This kernel is (topologically) generated by the elements V^m([x]) for m ≥ 0 and x ∈ I := ker(R^♭ → R).
sourceIssues.correction: The claim is false. The erratum states: 'The key step in the proof of Proposition 5.23 is to show that for a quasiregular semiperfect ring R, the divided Frobenius φ_1 acts topologically nilpotently on the kernel of the map A_crys(R) → W(R). This is not true.' The counterexample, due to Andrew Senger, is R = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/x with the element Σ_{k ∈ Z} p^k [x^{1/p^k}] of A_crys(R), which is fixed by the divided Frobenius and lies in the kernel of A_crys(R) → W(R). The erratum diagnoses the gap: 'While the generators of the kernel of A_crys(R) → W(R) used in the proof do topologically generate the kernel in the p-adic topology of A_crys(R), they fail to do so in the p-adic topology of the kernel itself.' The statement of Proposition 5.23 is unaffected: it was already known by the different proofs of Lau, Displays and formal p-divisible groups, and of Zink, The display of a formal p-divisible group, both cited immediately before it, and the erratum records that 'the arguments of this fallacious proof are not used anywhere else in the paper, so this mistake does not affect any of the results stated in the paper'.
